intended_object: The functor Π(X) → D induced, through the two-set Seifert–van Kampen universal property, by functors FA : Π(A) → D and FB : Π(B) → D that agree on Π(A ∩ B), when int A ∪ int B = X. In other words, the map out of the pushout Π(A) ⊔_{Π(A∩B)} Π(B) ≅ Π(X) (Brown, Topology and Groupoids, §6.7). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition applies the library's general gluing construction `TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoid.glue` to the cover of X by A and B, indexed by `Bool`. The hypothesis it passes, that every point has A or B as a neighbourhood, follows from `interior A ∪ interior B = univ`, which is the standard van Kampen hypothesis. Agreement on all pairwise intersections reduces to the single condition `h` on A ∩ B; the B ∩ A case goes through a swap. The target D is an arbitrary category, and there are no connectedness assumptions, so nothing is restricted beyond the classical two-set statement.

The companion lemmas confirm the docstring. `map_subtypeVal_comp_glueTwo_left` and `map_subtypeVal_comp_glueTwo_right` show the functor restricts to FA and FB, and `eq_glueTwo` shows it is the unique such functor. The library then uses it as the cocone descent map in `isPushout_fundamentalGroupoid`.

Calling this too narrow would be wrong. The two-set case is the standard form of the theorem, and the library also provides the general cover version (`glue`), so this is just a packaging of it. Mathlib has no van Kampen or gluing construction for fundamental groupoids.
